summary: The packed coordination skills document a prose HTML-comment review protocol that the coordination engine does not accept; the protocol the engine enforces (review wait / review record, schema fsgg.coord.review-wait/v1 and fsgg.coord.review-decision/v2) appears in no packed skill.
evidence: command:grep -rn 'review record|review wait' .claude/skills/ (returns nothing); command:scripts/fsgg-coord facts --json (reviewPolicy.schema = fsgg.coord.review-decision/v2); issue:EHotwagner/S.I.R.#255
cost: Blocked every PR in the workspace from reaching a landable green verdict; three PRs (#251, #253, #254) stalled simultaneously.

summary: A contract that is undocumented in prose was fully recoverable by calling the engine's own encoder and validator rather than guessing field values: ReviewWait.encode emits the exact wait document, Driver.encodeStructuredReview emits the exact record document, and StructuredDecision.validateReviewLedger names each invariant it enforces.
evidence: command:dotnet fsi with #r FS.GG.Coord.Core.dll calling ReviewWait.encode, Driver.encodeStructuredReview, StructuredDecision.validateReviewLedger
owner: FS-GG Kit — fs.gg.coord.cli; generalizable authoring guidance for any digest-sealed ledger

summary: The engine derives revision, previousDigest, claimGeneration, baseSha and digest from live state and overwrites whatever the draft supplied, so authoring a review record never requires inventing a sealed field; the absence of that fact from any documentation caused a prior worker to stop work believing the ledger could only be written with guessed values.
evidence: command:ilspycmd -t FS.GG.Coord.Cli.Client fsgg-coord-engine.dll (recordReview$cont@2412-3 rebuilds the record with existing.Length+1, previous, live claim id, live base tip sha, and StructuredDecision.reviewDigest); issue:EHotwagner/S.I.R.#255
cost: One item stopped mid-flight and escalated as unresolvable-locally; the blocking premise was false.
owner: S.I.R. — docs/coordination-engine-contracts.md and the packed independent-review contract

summary: validateReviewLedger refuses meaningful route evidence with the message 'meaningful route evidence must contain built artifact, command, comparison, and result', but the check is purely a cardinality test: any four strings pass and any other count fails, so the message describes semantics the validator does not enforce.
evidence: command:dotnet fsi calling StructuredDecision.validateReviewLedger with RouteEvidence ["a";"b";"c";"d"] (accepted) and with four descriptive strings (accepted) and with three or five (refused)
cost: Misleading refusal text invites an author to rewrite evidence content when only the count is wrong.

summary: scripts/fsgg-coord whoami --mint prints an export line for one shell only, and a harness that gives each tool call a fresh shell silently reverts the worker to the shared session identity, which is exactly the claim collision the mint exists to prevent; no packed skill states that the mint does not persist.
evidence: command:scripts/fsgg-coord whoami --mint (emits 'export FSGG_WORKER=...' and a note to eval it in EACH worker's shell); issue:EHotwagner/S.I.R.#255
cost: Silent identity reversion with no failure signal; every subsequent shell must re-export FSGG_WORKER explicitly.
